title: Security, past the headers
summary: What breaks a web app is rarely a zero-day. It is untrusted input reaching a parser that cannot tell data from code, a password stored with the wrong kind of hash, a token left where a script can read it, or a key that stopped being secret the moment the build finished. This is the half a web engineer builds and reviews; the headers section owns the header-shaped part, and neither section teaches an attack it does not need for the defence to make sense.
